messages:
kyle: Quick thread: for Private BYOK sidecar we need concrete controls so auditors get proof we never persist key material or raw key ids. Thoughts?
nina: Minimal list: one-way key fingerprints, deterministic redaction in logs, RBAC deny for export, cert-pinned mTLS to customer HSM.
sec-bot: CI rule: fail builds if any log line or env var contains /key(id|_id)?/i or looks like a raw key material blob.
flora: Operational: run sidecar unprivileged, seccomp profile, no debug symbols in production build, and mount no writable dirs for secrets. Use tenant-provided salt for hashing if they opt in.
ops: Audit schema: single-line JSON with ts, actor, op, key_fp, trace_id, result, proxy_ver. Store only key_fp (sha256) and never store salt. Provide export by trace_id for customers.
kyle: Incident playbook sketch: 1) detect anomalous calls 2) cordon tenant proxies 3) export hashed logs + trace ids 4) request HSM audit slice from customer 5) coordinate rotation of wrappers if needed 6) produce signed chain-of-custody report for SOC2.
nina: RBAC snippet: allow: [Encrypt,Decrypt,Sign]; explicit deny: [ExportKey,GetKeyMaterial,ImportKey]. Policies must reference hashed resource names only.
sec-bot: Add redaction middleware for headers like x-key-id and runtime env scrubbing. Also add test ensuring fingerprinting is non-reversible.
kyle: Action items: nina -> draft IAM JSON; flora -> seccomp profile + container hardening; ops -> audit schema + export endpoint; sec-bot -> CI checks. We'll add this to the sprint.
